title: Highest-weight modules of Weyl dimension by integral specialization
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], of prime characteristic $p>0$, and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Semisimple means smooth, affine, connected and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, where solvable means that the successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and central means commuting with every element after every scalar extension. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\ge0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$; a maximal torus is one not contained in a larger torus. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$. Use the character lattice $X=X^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots $\alpha^\vee$ and integer pairing of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $\eta\in X$ be dominant, meaning $\langle\eta,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for all $\alpha\in\Delta$, and let $\widetilde\eta:B\to\mathbf G_m$ be its extension trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$. There exist a finite-dimensional rational $S$-module $W$ and a nonzero vector $v\in W$ such that
$$b(v\otimes1)=\widetilde\eta(b)(v\otimes1)\quad\text{for every commutative }F\text{-algebra }D\text{ and }b\in B(D),$$
and
$$\dim_F W=\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\frac{\langle\eta+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle}{\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle}.$$
Here a rational module means a counital coassociative $F$-linear coaction $W\to W\otimes_F F[S]$, so the displayed eigenvector assertion is an identity of coactions, not only an assertion on $F$-points. The product is computed in $\mathbf Q$, with positive integer denominators, and equals the ordinary integer vector-space dimension. The empty product is $1$. No simplicity or realization by regular-function induction is required of $W$.

source.place: Characteristic-zero Weyl character formula, Theorem 22.52, printed p.480, restricted to characteristic zero; Section 23h, admissible lattices, equations (152)--(153) and Theorem 23.72, printed pp.509--511. Agent-formulated integral-specialization consequence, with the highest-weight direct summand retained on reduction. Supplementary WANTED: Jantzen, Representations of Algebraic Groups (2003), II.2.13, integral construction of Weyl modules. This is an existence statement for a rational module of Weyl dimension, not a dimension formula for the global induced module in positive characteristic.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice], the roots span $V=X\otimes\mathbf Q$ and $X$ is their full weight lattice $P$. Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding] to the given group root datum: its rational roots and coroot functionals are a reduced crystallographic root system in $V$; the central summand is zero. Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation] to obtain a split rational Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, splitting Cartan $\mathfrak h$ identified with $V^\vee$, and a Chevalley basis $h_i,e_\alpha$, together with an auxiliary faithful representation $A$ and full graded admissible lattice $\Lambda_A$. The weights of $A$ generate $P=X$. Use the specified positive roots throughout. If $V=0$, the same cited statements give $\mathfrak g=0$, $A=\mathbf Q$ and $\Lambda_A=\mathbf Z$, so the construction below includes this case.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.508--511, rational Chevalley data and full-weight auxiliary representation

proof.text: The given $\eta$ is in $P$ and is dominant for this rational Lie algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-highest-weight-modules] to obtain its finite-dimensional simple module $L=L(\eta)$ over $\mathbf Q$ and a cyclic highest vector $z\ne0$. Its finite weight set $\Omega$ is contained in $\eta-\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta$, and $z$ is killed by every positive root operator. Apply [lem-sfb-characteristic-zero-weyl-dimension] to $L$: its rational dimension $d$ is precisely the product in the item, with positive integer denominators. This invokes the dimension theorem only in characteristic zero.

source.place: Theorem 22.52, p.480 (characteristic zero only), and Section 23h, p.508 (rational split modules)

proof.text:
Let $U_{\mathbf Z}\subset U_{\mathbf Q}(\mathfrak g)$ be the divided-power subalgebra of [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw], and define the actual subgroup $\Lambda=U_{\mathbf Z}z\subset L$. Fix an ordering $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N$ of the positive roots. The cited integral triangular basis shows
$$\Lambda=\sum_{a\in\mathbf N^N}\mathbf Z\left(\prod_j e_{-\beta_j}^{(a_j)}\right)z.$$
Indeed every nonconstant positive factor kills $z$, and each Cartan binomial acts by the integer $\binom{\langle\eta,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle}{b_i}$; conversely each negative monomial lies in $U_{\mathbf Z}$. The rational span is $L$, since the rational span of $U_{\mathbf Z}$ contains the root vectors and their brackets $h_i$, and $z$ is cyclic by [lem-sfb-rational-highest-weight-modules]. Each root divided power preserves $\Lambda$ because $U_{\mathbf Z}$ is an algebra.

source.place: Section 23h, p.510, admissible lattice construction before (152); integral PBW input written out

proof.text: Each negative monomial in Step 3 is homogeneous of weight $\mu=\eta-\sum_j a_j\beta_j$, by $[h,e_{-\beta}]=-\beta(h)e_{-\beta}$. If its value is nonzero, $\mu\in\Omega$. With height denoting the sum of simple-root coordinates, choose $M=\max_{\mu\in\Omega}\operatorname{ht}(\eta-\mu)$. Since every positive root has height at least one, a surviving monomial has $\sum_j a_j\le M$. Thus only finitely many monomials survive. Grouping these homogeneous generators proves $\Lambda=\bigoplus_\mu\Lambda_\mu$, with $\Lambda_\mu=\Lambda\cap L_\mu$. The only monomial of weight $\eta$ is the empty monomial, since all positive-root heights are positive. Consequently $\Lambda_\eta=\mathbf Zz$ and $L_\eta=\mathbf Qz$, and $\mathbf Zz$ is a direct summand of $\Lambda$. For $N=0$ only the empty tuple occurs and these assertions still hold.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (152), p.510; explicit finite-generation and primitive highest-line verification

proof.text: In a rational basis of $L$, the finite set of lattice generators has rational coordinates. Choose one positive integer $c$ divisible by all their denominators. Then $c\Lambda\subseteq\mathbf Z^d$. By [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free], $\Lambda$ is free of finite rank. Its integer basis is rationally independent: multiplying a rational relation by a common denominator gives an integer relation. It rationally spans $L$ by Step 3, hence has exactly $d$ elements and $\Lambda\otimes\mathbf Q=L$. Each graded summand is likewise finite free, by the same subgroup theorem. Put $W=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbf Z}F$. Tensoring these chosen bases gives $\dim_F W=d$, and the direct summand $\mathbf Zz$ gives a nonzero vector $v=z\otimes1\in W$ and its one-dimensional weight summand.

source.place: Section 23h, p.510, full lattice and reduction $W(k)$; finite-free subgroup input

proof.text: Root operators on $L$ shift weights by their roots. Because $\Omega$ is finite and a nonzero rational root has distinct integer multiples, sufficiently many iterations of any root operator kill every weight space. Thus these operators are nilpotent. The representation on $A\oplus L$ with lattice $\Lambda_A\oplus\Lambda$ is faithful, its weights still generate $P$, and it satisfies all graded-lattice and divided-power conditions, by Steps 1--5. Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-root-exponential-group] to this representation over $F$. It gives a smooth connected semisimple closed subgroup $H\subseteq\operatorname{GL}((\Lambda_A\oplus\Lambda)\otimes F)$, with maximal torus $D_F(P)$ and exactly the given roots and coroots. Its generating matrices are the displayed root exponentials. Every such matrix is block diagonal, so the smallest closed subgroup they generate lies in the closed block-diagonal subgroup $\operatorname{GL}(\Lambda_A\otimes F)\times\operatorname{GL}(W)$. Projection to the second factor therefore gives a rational $H$-module structure on $W$. Its torus acts on $\Lambda_\mu\otimes F$ by the actual character $\mu$, not by its differential.

source.place: Section 23h, equations (152)--(153) and Theorem 23.72, pp.510--511; apply the full-weight construction to an auxiliary direct sum

proof.text: Both $S$ and $H$ are reductive by the semisimple clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Their identified torus character lattices are $X=P$ and their roots and coroots agree. Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-isogeny-realization] with $G_1=S$, $G_0=H$, lattice map $u=\operatorname{id}_X$, root bijection the identity, and every root exponent equal to $1$. Its isomorphism criterion gives an isomorphism $f:S\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ whose torus pullback is this identity. Pull back the representation of Step 6 along $f$. This is a rational $S$-action on $W$, and its $T$-weight summands are exactly those from Steps 4--6. In particular all weights are $\eta$ or strictly below $\eta$ in the positive-root order, and $W_\eta=Fv$.

source.place: Theorems 23.25 and 23.72, pp.492--493 and 510--511; prescribed-root-datum identification

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], the specified $B$ is $P(
u)$ for a regular cocharacter $
u:\mathbf G_m	o T$. Its tangent description gives $\langle\alpha,
uangle>0$ on every positive root. Thus every weight $\mu
e\eta$ of $W$ has $\langle\mu-\eta,
uangle<0$. Choose a weight basis of $W$ containing $v$. For every commutative $F$-algebra $D$ and $b\in B(D)$, the matrix of $
u(t)b
u(t)^{-1}$ extends to $t=0$, by the definition of $P(
u)$. Its entry from $v$ to a weight-$\mu$ basis vector is $t^{\langle\mu-\eta,
uangle}$ times the corresponding entry of $b$. A Laurent monomial of negative exponent belongs to $D[t]$ only if its coefficient is zero, also when $D$ has nilpotents. All these entries vanish. Hence $B$ preserves $Dv$ for every $D$. Applying the same argument to $b^{-1}$ shows that the scalar is a unit; taking $D=F[B]$ gives a group-scheme character $\chi:B	o\mathbf G_m$ with $b(v\otimes1)=\chi(b)(v\otimes1)$ and $\chi|_T=\eta$.

source.place: Section 22a, highest-weight line; elementary cocharacter matrix verification using the Borel description

proof.text: Write $U=R_u(B)$. By [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], $U$ is isomorphic as an $F$-scheme to $\mathbf A_F^{|\Phi^+|}$. The restriction of $\chi$ to $U$ is therefore a unit in a polynomial ring over $F$ and so is a constant: degrees of nonzero polynomials add under multiplication, whereas a polynomial times its inverse has degree zero. Its value at the identity is $1$, so $\chi|_U=1$ as an equality of regular functions, hence after every $D$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], multiplication identifies $B=U\rtimes T$. Since $\chi|_T=\eta$ and $\chi|_U=1$, it equals the stated extension $\widetilde\eta$. Step 8 is therefore precisely the required coaction eigenvector identity.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), p.510, and Section 22a; scheme-theoretic Borel eigencharacter verification

proof.text: The underlying space of this representation remains $W=\Lambda\otimes F$. Step 5 gives its dimension $d$ and $v\ne0$, and Step 2 identifies $d$ with the specified rational product. Together with Step 9 this proves both assertions. In rank zero, the construction gives $W=F$ and $v=1$ with the trivial action, and both dimensions and the empty product equal $1$. No simplicity assertion about the reduction has been used.
